page.layout: One printed page. Full-width ornament rule at top, then heading "Errata.", then one block of errata text in paragraphs, then a centred closing line, then "FINIS" in spaced capitals. Faint show-through from the reverse page is visible and not transcribed.

main_text.head: Errata.
main_text.p: Pag. 6. lin. 12. ἐγένετο Pag. 28. lin. 3. lege asscri-bam. pag. 57. lin. 1. sagen. p. 63. l. 23. lege res illa. pag. 82. lin. 12. lege egeat. p. 90. lin. 11. lege ὀρθο-δόξον. p. 109. lin. 13. lege hominum. pag. 114. lin. 11. lege his verbis. pag. 135. lin. 3. lege putidissimo. pag. 149. lin. 15. lege articuli. p. 150. lin. 6. lege pagina pag. 183. lin. 10. & 11. lege evulgata, excusa. pag. 193. lin. 1. lege patribus. p. 220. lin. 5. lege jejunaveruntq. p. 238. lin. penultimâ lege faciem. pag. 277. lin. 6. naturæ humanæ pag. 278. lin. 7. lege pestes. ibid. lin. 10. de le & ibid. lin. 12. leg. omnes.
Et alia quædam benevolus lector excusset & corrigat.

page.notes: The Greek words "ἐγένετο" and "ὀρθοδόξον" are printed as shown; the Greek in "ὀρθο-δόξον" is split across a line end. "sagen." at pag. 57 is printed as a fragment of a German-looking word; the reading is doubtful. The printed "excusset" in the closing line appears as "excusset" in the scan and is shown as printed. The closing line "Et alia quædam benevolus lector excusset" may read "excuset" in the original; the scan is partly ambiguous. The ornament rule and the closing "FINIS" are set apart and not transcribed as text beyond the word itself.
